title: Comparison of corneal endothelial changes following phacoemulsification in diabetic and non-diabetic patients

license.statement: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (article <license>); not CC BY, record kept private

indication: Senile nuclear cataract grade I-III; diabetic group with type 2 diabetes and good glycaemic control (HbA1c below 7%) without diabetic retinopathy, non-diabetic group age-matched; corneal disease, pseudoexfoliation, glaucoma, uveitis, retinal disease and previous ocular surgery excluded

groups.description: Phacoemulsification (phaco chop, single surgeon) in patients without diabetes
Phacoemulsification (phaco chop, single surgeon) in patients with type 2 diabetes
groups.indication: senile cataract with type 2 diabetes (patient-condition subgroup)

notes: Prospective comparative observational study of 200 patients (100 per group), one operated eye per patient as implied by group sizes and side counts.
The second postoperative visit is labelled '4-weeks' in the Table 3 rows and in the abstract but '1 month' in the caption and Methods; it is converted as 4 weeks (28 days).
Table 5 (BCVA) reports n = 100 per group at every visit; the ECD table gives no per-visit n.
Both groups receive the same standard surgery; diabetes defines a patient-condition subgroup, so both are control.
